text:
elena: Quick heads-up — I kicked off the quarterly credential ownership verification. KMS scan flagged ~14 keys with no owner label and a couple of service accounts with stale keys. Need owners + evidence (who/why/how used) by EOW so we can decide rotate vs decommission. tagging @oliver oncall for immediate triage.

oliver: ack. Can you drop the list? I can start paging teams for anything that looks like critical infra.

elena: pasted CSV excerpt below (sanitized):
```
key_id,project,usage_hint,last_seen,label_owner
k-9f3e,infra-prod,db-migrator,2026-02-14,
k-3a7b,metrics,stackdriver-exporter,2025-12-01,
k-1c2d,auth,svc-legacy-auth,2024-08-03,
```
I'll upload full report to the shared folder: https://redwood.internal/secure/cred-reports/q1-2026 (access: eng-security only)

ria: thanks. runbook reminder: for each key we need either: owner claim (slack + audit ticket), documented use (runbook or PR referencing key id), or rotation plan. If none, mark for scheduled revoke + rotate. I can seed the ticket template.

matt: small automation note — we can kick the claim flow via the ownership API: `POST /internal/ownership/claims` with payload `{"key_id":"k-9f3e","claimer":"team-name","evidence_url":"..."}`. I can wire a button in the report page if teams want to self-claim.

oliver: nice. For oncall urgent hits (keys used by services in the last 30d with no owner) we should error-budget whitelist 24h and page owners. Which ones are in that bucket?

elena: two keys with last_seen < 30d: k-9f3e and k-3a7b. k-9f3e looks high-risk (db migrator). I left a note in the CSV for priority.

oliver: paging infra leads: @mike-infra and @sara-db, please confirm ownership or we will rotate after 24h. :warning:

inc-bot: AUTOMATED SCAN: 14 orphaned keys detected. Opened eng-security ticket #SEC-5421. Evidence deadline: 72h.

ria: small compliance ask — please attach audit evidence to ticket as a link (runbook PR, support ticket, or commit). If it's a temporary key for a canary/experiment, tag with expiry and responsible engineer.

elena: also flagging a subtle KMS integration issue: our label-sync job missed some keys because the service account that writes labels hit quota on the API. Filed infra issue #INFRA-3109. Will follow up.

matt: noted. For the immediate cleanup path I propose: 1) attempt owner claim flow for all 14; 2) for unclaimed keys with last_seen > 90d, schedule revoke+rotation 7d after notice; 3) for keys last_seen < 30d, require explicit owner confirmation or emergency rollback plan.

oliver: +1. I'll start paging and escalate if we don't get confirmations. If anyone wants to pair on the automation button, I can help this afternoon.

elena: thanks — I'll update the shared sheet with the action column and set reminders. tagging followups in #eng-security-checkins for audit trace. :thumbsup:

ria: adding compliance checklist to SEC-5421 now.

oliver: quick Q — what about service accounts that appear unused but have long-lived tokens? Should we rotate tokens before revoking keys?

elia: (typo) meant to say: elena: good catch — if token/token-like credentials exist, rotate tokens first to avoid outages, then rotate keys. We'll coordinate with app owners.

matt: I'll add a pre-rotation smoke test to SEC-5421 so owners can opt-in.

elena: OK closing the loop here. Will post a status update in 12h with owners reached. If anyone finds a secret reference in a repo, ping me directly.

oliver: thanks all. :eyes:
